newsitem.title: CHINA: China says U.N. human rights censure doomed.
newsitem.headline: China says U.N. human rights censure doomed.

text.p: Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen said on Friday any attempt to censure China at the U.N. Human Rights Commission for human rights abuses was doomed to fail.

"If they insist on doing the same this year, the outcome will be the same as in the past," Qian told reporters when asked to comment on a possible move to censure China at a commission meeting in Geneva for human rights violations.

China will likely escape censure for the seventh year in a row at the United Nations forum, which opens on Monday, because Washington and Brussels have been lax in lobbying for support for a resolution, according to Amnesty International delegates.

On Thursday, the London-based human rights watchdog group Amnesty International accused the United States and European Union of protecting violators from scrutiny by the U.N. Human Rights Commission -- including China, Indonesia, Saudi Arabia and Turkey.
In its latest annual report on human rights, the U.S. State Department accused Beijing of effectively silencing public dissent in 1996 through jailings, intimidation or exile.
China considers dissidents like Wei Jingsheng, dubbed the father of China's modern democracy movement and a nominee of the Nobel Peace Prize, as common criminals.
